risk.title: 32-bit worker process enabled
risk.comment: A 32-bit worker process has a substantially smaller user-mode address space and can encounter out-of-memory failures earlier than a 64-bit process.
risk.recommendation: Confirm that 32-bit dependencies require this setting and correlate memory pressure with private bytes, virtual bytes, and crash evidence.

risk.title: Application pool queue length increased
risk.comment: A larger queue can retain more waiting requests, increasing latency and memory pressure while masking downstream saturation.
risk.recommendation: Validate sustained throughput, request latency, HTTPERR QueueFull records, and the capacity of downstream dependencies.

risk.title: Application pool queue length reduced
risk.comment: A smaller queue can reject bursts sooner and may increase HTTP 503 responses when worker processes are saturated or starting.
risk.recommendation: Correlate with HTTPERR QueueFull records and confirm that the reduced limit is intentional.

risk.title: Rapid-Fail Protection disabled
risk.comment: Repeated worker-process crashes may continue without the application pool being stopped, increasing churn and resource consumption.
risk.recommendation: Confirm why crash-loop protection is disabled and review WAS and Application event logs for repeated failures.

risk.title: Worker-process user profile loading enabled
risk.comment: Profile loading can affect startup, registry access, temporary paths, and resource usage for the application pool identity.
risk.recommendation: Verify that the application requires a user profile and correlate profile service warnings with pool startup failures.

risk.title: Web garden enabled
risk.comment: Multiple worker processes can duplicate in-process cache and session state and complicate request affinity and memory analysis.
risk.recommendation: Confirm the application is designed for multiple worker processes and does not depend on in-process state.

risk.title: Periodic recycle interval customized
risk.comment: Custom recycle timing can cause cold starts or interrupt long-running work at a schedule that differs from the IIS default.
risk.recommendation: Correlate recycle events with traffic and ensure overlapped recycling and application warm-up are appropriate.

risk.title: Request body limit increased
risk.comment: Allowing larger request bodies can increase upload time, disk use, and memory or bandwidth pressure.
risk.recommendation: Confirm the business requirement and align proxy, ASP.NET, and application-level request limits.

risk.title: Double escaping allowed
risk.comment: Allowing double-escaped URL sequences broadens accepted input and can weaken path and request validation assumptions.
risk.recommendation: Keep disabled unless a verified application requirement exists and test canonicalization and authorization behavior.

risk.title: Directory browsing enabled
risk.comment: Directory listings can disclose file names, application structure, backups, or other unintended content.
risk.recommendation: Disable unless directory listing is an explicit feature and confirm authorization boundaries.

risk.title: Detailed IIS errors enabled
risk.comment: Detailed errors can expose implementation and environment information to clients.
risk.recommendation: Use detailed errors only in controlled troubleshooting scopes and return generic errors to remote production clients.

risk.title: ARR proxy enabled
risk.comment: The server is acting as a reverse proxy, so timeout, buffering, affinity, and upstream health settings can affect availability and latency.
risk.recommendation: Review proxy timeouts, preserve-host-header requirements, upstream health, and forwarded-header trust.

risk.title: Basic authentication enabled
risk.comment: Basic authentication transmits reusable credentials and requires TLS protection for every request path.
risk.recommendation: Require HTTPS, disable plaintext access, and confirm credential delegation and storage requirements.

risk.title: Windows Authentication enabled
risk.comment: Windows Authentication changes the request identity flow and can introduce repeated challenges, delegation constraints, and Kerberos or NTLM dependency issues.
risk.recommendation: Review providers, kernel-mode settings, SPNs, delegation, application-pool identity, and 401 substatus evidence.

risk.title: Anonymous authentication enabled
risk.comment: Anonymous access may be expected for public sites but can expose resources if authorization rules are incomplete.
risk.recommendation: Confirm authorization rules and filesystem permissions for every anonymous application path.

risk.title: ASP.NET debug compilation enabled
risk.comment: Debug compilation increases execution overhead, disables important optimizations, and can extend request timeouts.
risk.recommendation: Disable in production and rebuild with production diagnostics and symbol handling.

risk.title: ASP.NET execution timeout increased
risk.comment: Long execution timeouts can retain blocked requests and associated resources for longer during dependency failures.
risk.recommendation: Confirm the workload requires the higher timeout and correlate with request queues, thread usage, and downstream latency.

risk.title: ASP.NET request size limit increased
risk.comment: Larger managed request bodies can increase memory, disk, and bandwidth pressure.
risk.recommendation: Align this limit with IIS requestFiltering and enforce application-specific upload validation.

risk.title: In-process ASP.NET session state
risk.comment: Session data consumes worker-process memory and is lost on recycle or crash; large sessions can amplify memory growth.
risk.recommendation: Measure session size and growth, and consider an out-of-process provider when resilience or scale-out is required.

risk.title: ASP.NET custom errors disabled
risk.comment: Detailed exception information may be returned to remote clients.
risk.recommendation: Use RemoteOnly or On in production and preserve detailed diagnostics in protected server-side logs.

risk.title: HttpOnly cookies disabled
risk.comment: Client-side script can access cookies that do not set HttpOnly, increasing impact if script injection occurs.
risk.recommendation: Enable HttpOnly for cookies that do not require script access.

risk.title: Secure cookies not required
risk.comment: Cookies may be sent over unencrypted HTTP when the application is reachable without strict HTTPS enforcement.
risk.recommendation: Require HTTPS and Secure cookies for production authentication and session data.

risk.title: ASP.NET impersonation enabled
risk.comment: Request execution identity changes can broaden access paths and make authorization and auditing harder to reason about.
risk.recommendation: Verify the intended identity flow, least-privilege permissions, and delegation boundaries.

risk.title: ASP.NET tracing enabled
risk.comment: Tracing can expose request, control, cookie, header, and server details and adds runtime overhead.
risk.recommendation: Disable after troubleshooting and restrict local-only access while enabled.
